prerequisites: It is highly recommended that students have passed Fluid Mechanics and Fluid Mechanics Machines and Systems.
Knowledge of the fundamental equations of basic mechanics and thermodynamics.
Concepts of energy equation and head loss.

Basic knowledge of Theory of machines and mechanisms, Machine Calculation and Design, Strength of Materials, Manufacturing Processes, Manufacturing Engineering, Graphic Expression and Automation and Control.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the basic principles of Fluid Mechanics and its application to solving problems in the field of Engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid mechanical systems and machines.
Understand and apply the fundamentals of oleohydraulic and pneumatic drive systems.
Assemble and test the performance and operation of oleohydraulic and pneumatic circuits.
Perform operation, regulation and maintenance tasks of oleohydraulic and pneumatic systems.
Design, calculate and project oleohydraulic and pneumatic drive systems.
Manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards in relation to oleohydraulic and pneumatic systems.

syllabus_topics: Symbolism, hydraulic fluids and compressed air
Design and project of oleohydraulic systems
Compressed air generation, distribution and conditioning systems
Actuators. Proportional valves and automatic processes
Design and project of pneumatic systems

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices and active student participation (EV-3+EV-4)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.7 × Theoretical Exam (EV-1) + 0.15 × Exercises and Works (EV-2) + 0.15 × (Laboratory Practices + Participation) (EV-3+EV-4). A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for EV-1 to pass; otherwise, the final grade is capped at 4.0. For the extraordinary call, if no complementary activities were done, the exam is weighted at 70%, with a maximum possible grade of 7.0 and a minimum of 4 to pass. Differentiated evaluation uses a formula of 0.9 × Theoretical Exam (EV-1) + 0.1 × Activities Test (EV-2), also requiring a minimum of 4 in EV-1.
